correctness.rationale: The 3- and 5-color cyclic periodicity proofs are complete, with all bounds explicit for n≥7. For four colors, consecutive-triple properness and consecutive-five-window colorfulness are equivalent to the fall condition. Closed length-n state walks bijectively enumerate labeled colorings. The 48-dimensional integer determinant identity is verified coefficient-by-coefficient by a standalone exact Newton-identity checker; the generating relation is formal. Direct base words for lengths 8,9,10,15 and insertion of a distinct 4-block establish all lengths ≥8 except 11; exact transfer counts exclude 7 and 11. Independently exhaustive direct colorings corroborate orders 7..16; these tests are not substituted for infinite proof.

evidence: Kumar–Nicholas–Somasundaram 2011, Theorem 6: for the square of a cycle, a maximum fall five-coloring exists exactly when the order is divisible by five.

Wang–Wen–Wang–Li 2024 studies general edge-count/density lower bounds, graph-colorability complexity, and planar construction classes; its neighborhood-density sufficiency hypothesis for four colors fails on degree-four cycle squares of n≥7.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2011 theorem strictly covers the five-color clause, and that clause is acknowledged as known; neither it nor a general density or complexity theorem yields the four-class cardinality sequence or the 7/11 forbidden orders. A broad chromatic polynomial counts proper colorings but does not enforce every vertex seeing each other color.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete enumeration of all fall color-class partitions on every squared cycle, not a one-off graph parameter or small census. It gives the entire allowed palette spectrum, a degree-48 rational count of four-class partitions, and a sharp unexplained-before pair of orders having no fall coloring. The structural 4-block insertion supplies a reusable explanation of its all-order threshold.
